previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, chronic back pain, and a history of anxiety was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and hyperglycemia. Her symptoms were triggered by back pain and anxiety, leading to poor oral intake and elevated blood glucose. She was treated with IV fluids for hypovolemia and hyponatremia, insulin therapy adjusted to avoid hypoglycemia, and lorazepam for anxiety. Her nausea resolved, and she tolerated a normal diet. Back pain was managed with acetaminophen, tizanidine, and a single dose of oxycodone. She was discharged on increased Lantus insulin, with recommendations to follow up with endocrinology, pain management, and mental health services to prevent recurrent admissions.

Brief Hospital Course:
Patient is a ___ yo woman with DM1 and frequent admissions for 
nausea/vomiting/abdominal pain presents with recurrent nausea, 
vomiting, and worsening back pain.  As usual, she improved with 
IV Zofran.  Her diet was advanced the following day to regular 
diabetic diet, which she tolerated well.  She was recommended to 
try to take Ativan instead of Zofran ODT as this was not helping 
her at home.  Her blood sugars are fairly well controlled, 
except for episode of hypoglycemia early morning, corrected with 
food intake.  Her insulin regimen remained unchanged from prior 
at discharge.  For her back pain, she was started on gabapentin.

it had not helped her.  Previously, she felt that the lidocaine 
patch had helped take the edge off her pain.  However, she could 
not get prior approval without trying gabapentin.  Thus, she 
will have a trial of gabapentin.  Of note, she is transitioning 
her care to ___, including establishing care with the Chronic 
Pain Service here for other pain control options.

You were started on gabapentin 200 mg three times a day for your

by 200 mg every week until you are taking a total of 400 mg 
three times a day.  For example, if you still have bad back pain 
next week, please take 400 mg in the morning, 200 mg in the 
early afternoon, and 200 mg before bed.  If you still have pain 
the following week, then increase your dose to 400 mg in the 
morning, 400 mg in the early afternoon, and 200 mg before bed.
